messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Smart-routing anomaly detected in prod (eu-west-1). Elevated error rate and misrouted variants. Paging oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging @trent (primary oncall) — please respond.
trent: on it. any impact visible to customers? where's the alert coming from?
maya: saw spike around +00:42 UTC. traffic started routing to `redwood-4b-legacy` instead of `redwood-4b-quant` for a subset of sessions. latency + error-rate up ~3x for those requests.
zoe: I can confirm a handful of enterprise sessions showed hallucination patterns after being served by legacy variant. CS flagged 2 customers already.
alan: FYI I rolled out a small policy tweak 2h ago to the fallback matrix (allow cross-region fallback threshold=0.2). change was successful but might explain cross-region chatter.
trent: pushing logs. can someone paste the routing decision logs for a sample request? I want to check route tags.
maya: pasting a snippet — note: `route_tag` missing in a few entries.
```
DECISION_LOG: {
  request_id: "r-7f2a9",
  source_region: "eu-west-1",
  selected_variant: "redwood-4b-legacy",
  fallback_reason: "capacity_unavailable",
  route_tag: null,
  decision_path: ["primary", "policy_fallback", "region_swap"]
}
```
trent: hmm. route_tag null. we expect `route_tag` to be set to e.g. `variant_v2` or `pinned_region=eu`. if missing, observability won't attribute which policy branch triggered the decision.
ops-rotation: is this a logging bug or the policy returned an empty tag? both possible. we should instrument quickly before more customers are affected.
cs-liaison: customer impact: 3 enterprise accounts reported increased latency (avg 6.2s) and one reported a content regression — asking for ETA and mitigation steps.
trent: mitigation plan idea: temporary disable cross-region fallback for prod-eu and pin variants for high-tier customers. can we do a scoped override?
alan: we have `routing.override` API. sample: `rdctl routing override --scope=prod:eu-west-1 --policy allow_cross_region=false --reason "incident 1977654321"`
zoe: recommend also add a safety rule to force `route_tag` onto decision write so we can trace the rest of the requests while we work. low risk change: append `route_tag=override-pin` in the decision write path.
trent: agree. steps: 1) apply scoped override, 2) add tag-on-write, 3) monitor client errors/latency, 4) gradual rollback if stable. who can apply override now?
alan: I can do override within 2 min. executing: `rdctl routing override --scope=prod:eu-west-1 --policy allow_cross_region=false --reason "mitigate misrouting"`
alan: (executed) override applied. changes propagate to routing layer in ~30s.
maya: seeing immediate drop in cross-region spikes, selected_variant now mostly `redwood-4b-quant`. error-rate for affected buckets down 65% within 3 min.
zoe: deploying a tiny decision-write patch to ensure `route_tag` not null for fallback branches. patch is trivial; toggling feature flag `fix/route-tag-on-decisions`.
trent: hold — we should be careful touching decision write path in prod during a live incident. can we enable the flag in staging first?
zoe: yep, tested in staging — writes now include `route_tag: "policy_override_pin"` for fallback cases. enabling feature-flag in prod (read-only change in obs path).
zoe: (enabled) flag turned on for prod. decision logs now show tags. sample: 
```
DECISION_LOG: {
  request_id: "r-7f3b1",
  source_region: "eu-west-1",
  selected_variant: "redwood-4b-quant",
  fallback_reason: "policy_override",
  route_tag: "policy_override_pin",
  decision_path: ["primary", "policy_override"]
}
```
trent: nice. this will help root cause and postmortem. cs-liaison: pinging customers that we're investigating, some mitigation applied, and will follow up with RCA.
cs-liaison: sent initial note to accounts A, B, C — asked if they'd like rollback to previous stable behavior; all asked to keep throughput but prefer correct variant.
ops-rotation: monitoring SLOs and error dashboards. sending alert if error-rate > 1.5x baseline on any customer.
maya: quick note: logs show a rare path where policy eval returns an empty `tag` when fallback chain uses a default policy object. root cause candidate: policy-loader returns `tag==""` for default entries.
trent: action items so far:
- alan: keep override in place until we confirm stability (done).
- zoe: coordinate with eng-runtime to bake non-null route_tag into decision writes (flag enabled, but need permanent fix).
- maya: run a targeted query for requests with `route_tag: null` over the last 6h and export sample ids.
- cs-liaison: customer comms + escalate to account execs.
ops-rotation: placing a temporary pager threshold suppression for noisy alerts during mitigation window.
alan: keeping an eye on capacity — we disabled cross-region fallback which can cause capacity pressure; if we see queueing, will enable limited burst fallback.
trent: after 25m of override + tag writes, metrics look good. routing stability improved, customer latency trending back to baseline.
cs-liaison: customers A/B replied: improved, thanks. they want RCA.
trent: opening a follow-up ticket for postmortem and instrumentation backlog: make `route_tag` required at policy evaluation time, add an end-to-end test for fallback tagging, and add a routing-decision trace view to console.
zoe: +1. also recommend adding a rollout guard for policy changes that don't set a `tag` field.
trench: handing off to zoe for the next 4h oncall. zoe: taking handoff. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-rotation: closing incident page; please add any follow-up tasks to the incident board `INC-1977654321`.
trent: ack — good job team.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation in place, monitoring. follow-up postmortem required.
